title: The exported service reads dates in the training order and says when it guessed
request: The owner asked for live checks of the new changes and to fix the date bugs the export check found.
spec: Dates read the way the training data wrote them; a guessed order or an unreadable date is said on its row; the capture's parity check reads dates the same way.
plan: learn the training order at capture
read with it in the scorer

decisions.decision: Warn, never refuse, on an ambiguous date
decisions.why: a service that refuses every 07/08 date fails real callers; a warning on the row tells them to send ISO dates

change: dclab_rnd/studio/service.py (date_order, time_dayfirst in model.json, the parity reader), dclab_rnd/studio/service_template/scorer.py (read_times, warnings on predictions), tests/test_service_dates.py, dclab_rnd/agent_eval/export_parity_live.py.

findings.defect: A day-first date was read month first with no warning.
findings.scenario: pr10's booking_date 07/08/2025 read as 8 July; the score moved from 0.2398 to 0.2877.
findings.fix: the training order learnt at capture and used; an ambiguous date warned

findings.defect: An unreadable date was scored as missing in silence.
findings.scenario: booking_date 'not a date' returned a score of 0.213.

measurements.name: End-to-end export parity on two practice projects (rules arm, no model)
measurements.result: pr10 roc_auc recorded 0.727288, service 0.727288; pr02 mae recorded 0.498861, service 0.498861; CSV and JSON identical
measurements.next: run the HTTP layer once Flask is installed
limits: the Flask layer itself not run (not installed)

outcome: The exported model reproduces the approved holdout score exactly on real rows; dates are now read in the training order and a guess is said.
lessons: A functional end-to-end run on real rows finds what synthetic parity rows cannot.
risks: pr02's exported model needs late_fee_charged, a planted late column the unattended plan did not catch (leaks by data, fix 3, still open).
